name: Turnbook
positioning: Fictional lesson for the 3x3 puzzle cube. It teaches the seven-stage layer-by-layer method on a cube the reader can turn, one turn at a time. Used to study a teaching page with an interactive 3D object.
audience: People who own a 3x3 cube, have never solved it, and want to follow along with the real cube in their hands.
voice: Say which face turns and which way, in plain words beside the notation
One instruction per line, numbers and colours named
Warn before a step looks wrong, such as the lower layers mixing in the last stage

direction.concept: A lesson book that turns. The cube is the page: every instruction shows on the cube as a violet arrow around the layer that turns next, and the lesson waits for you.
direction.tier: Tactile teaching tool. One three.js cube drawn in code beside a lesson panel; no scroll scene. Category measured 2026-10-17 (ruwix, cubeskills, grubiks, twizzle, rubiks-cube-solver, speedcubeshop): white or light grey pages, blue links and buttons, system fonts. Turnbook keeps the light page and moves the accent to violet, the one hue that is no sticker colour.
devices: A violet arc around the layer that turns next, with an arrowhead showing the direction
Notation set as mono keycaps, the current turn filled violet and done turns faded
Pieces that a step moves keep their colour; the rest dim
invariants: Violet means the next turn and the action; no sticker is ever violet
Every turn shows its notation and its plain words
The lesson is held white on top, green in front, then turned over once
variables: Sticker shades within the standard colour scheme

imagery.subject: One 3x3 puzzle cube with rounded black plastic pieces and the six standard sticker colours, floating over a soft shadow
imagery.materials: Satin black plastic, slightly glossy stickers, grey metal springs inside
imagery.lighting: Soft room light with a key from the upper right; no coloured light, so sticker colours stay true
imagery.palette: Stickers white #f4f2ec, yellow #ffd23a, green #0c9450, blue #1f5fd1, red #d12b3b, orange #ff7a1a; plastic #1b1a20; arrows violet #5b3df5
invariants: Standard scheme: white opposite yellow, green opposite blue, red opposite orange, red-white-blue clockwise at a corner
No logo, maker name or lettering on any piece
Drawn in code; no model files
avoid: The marks, logo or centre cap of any cube maker
Violet stickers or violet light on the cube

motion.character: Quarter turns take about a quarter second and ease out like a real layer clicking into place. The pieces gather from apart on load. A solved cube makes one slow lap of the view.
motion.reducedMotion: Turns jump to their end with the lesson's pauses kept, the pieces start together, and the solved cube does not spin.

chapters.question: How do I solve this cube?
chapters.message: Seven stages, each a few short algorithms, shown one turn at a time.
chapters.visual: The cube with a violet arc on the next layer, the lesson panel with the turns as keycaps.
chapters.transition: Each turn animates on the cube; the panel moves to the next keycap.
chapters.mobileFallback: Cube on top, lesson below, turn buttons under the cube.

chapters.question: What holds it together?
chapters.message: A core of three axes holds six centres; edges and corners hook under them.
chapters.visual: The pieces pull apart from the core and its springs, with labels.
chapters.transition: Pieces slide out along their own direction and back.

evidence.fact: The cube has 26 visible pieces: 6 centres fixed to a core of three intersecting axes, 12 edges and 8 corners; springs keep the pieces tensioned, and each piece has a concealed inward extension that interlocks with the others.
Face turns reach 43,252,003,274,489,856,000 arrangements, and any of them can be solved in 20 moves or fewer (proved in 2010).
Standard colour scheme: white opposite yellow, blue opposite green, orange opposite red; red, white and blue run clockwise.
Beginner method stages and algorithms: F R U R' U' F', R U R' U R U2 R' U, U R U' L' U R' U' L, R' D' R D, and the middle-layer pair U R U' R' U' F' U F and U' L' U L U F U' F'.
